title: The highest-fiber seeds

seo.title: Highest-fiber seeds: chia, flax, sesame and more
seo.meta_description: Chia and flax clearly lead for fiber. Compare grams per 100 g and per realistic serving to see how much they add.
seo.search_intent: Compare common seeds by fiber content and translate the ranking into realistic portions.

excerpt: Chia provides about 34 g of fiber per 100 g and flax about 27 g, well ahead of sesame, sunflower, pumpkin and hulled hemp. In a 20 g portion, chia contributes roughly 6.8 g of fiber and flax about 5.4 g, so this ranking has a genuinely large practical gap.
content_html:
The seeds that rank highest for protein are not the same ones that lead for fiber. Hemp and pumpkin seeds are protein-dense; chia and flax are the clear fiber standouts.

Because 100 g is a large amount of seeds, the table also shows a 20 g portion.

Fiber in common seeds

SeedFiber/100 gFiber in 20 g
Chia~34 g~6.8 g
Flax~27 g~5.4 g
Sesame~12 g~2.4 g
Sunflower~8.6 g~1.7 g
Pumpkin~6 g~1.2 g
Hulled hemp~4 g~0.8 g

This is not a ranking decided by tiny decimal differences. Twenty grams of chia can provide roughly five times as much fiber as the same weight of hulled pumpkin seeds.

Why chia turns into a gel

Chia's outer layer contains fiber that holds water and forms a mucilage gel. That explains the texture change in chia pudding and soaked seeds. Chia still contains both soluble and insoluble fiber; the gel does not mean all of its fiber is soluble.

Flax is fiber-rich, but grinding matters

Whole flax seeds can pass through the digestive tract partly intact. Grinding them makes the interior more accessible, including alpha-linolenic acid, while preserving their fiber.

A 20 g portion supplies about 5.4 g of fiber, not the 27 g shown by a 100 g comparison.

High-protein seeds are not automatically high-fiber seeds

Hulled hemp and pumpkin seeds can provide around 30 g of protein per 100 g but far less fiber than chia or flax. Removing hulls also removes some of the fiber-rich outer structure.

That means different seeds solve different nutritional problems: hemp and pumpkin seeds are useful for protein, while chia and flax are much stronger fiber additions.

Increase fiber gradually

Adding several tablespoons of chia or flax overnight to a previously low-fiber diet can cause gas, bloating or bowel changes. Increasing gradually and drinking enough fluid is usually more comfortable.

The practical answer

Chia and flax are the two clear fiber leaders among common seeds. A modest portion can add roughly 5–7 g of fiber, while other seeds stand out for different nutrients.

faq.question: Which seed has the most fiber?
faq.answer: Chia is near the top at about 34 g of fiber per 100 g, followed by flax at roughly 27 g.

faq.question: How much fiber is in 20 g of chia?
Are hemp seeds high in fiber?
faq.answer: Hulled hemp is high in protein but relatively low in fiber, often around 4 g per 100 g depending on the product.
